Serving the Piedmont from Forest to Concord

Forest, Madison Heights, Rustburg, Amherst, Bedford, Appomattox and Concord

One hillside through the year

Leaf-off (Nov–Mar)

Hardwoods visible, ground firm. Prime window for clearing slopes.

Spring rain (Apr–May)

Red clay slick. Mulch over doze so the bank holds.

Summer resprout (Jun–Aug)

Follow-up visit for invasives. Mowing returns.

Fall grass (Sep–Oct)

Field comes back. Broomsedge gold. Fence rows open.

What we clear and how

  • Old field and pasture reclaiming

    Grown-up hayfields and pastures opened back to grass, cedars and briars gone.

    Price it

  • Forestry mulching

    Brush and saplings mulched on steep ground where a dozer would tear the hill.

    Price it

  • Homesite clearing on sloped lots

    A house spot and drive cut into the hillside, with the slope kept from washing.

    Price it

  • Fence row and hedgerow clearing

    Old fence rows grown into tree lines cut back so new fence can go in.

    Price it

  • Invasive plant removal

    Tree of heaven, autumn olive and multiflora rose cut and kept from coming back.

    Price it

  • Farm road and trail cutting

    Woods roads and walking trails reopened along the contour so they hold up.

    Price it

  • Stump grinding

    Stumps ground out of yards and field edges so you can mow right across.

    Price it

  • Tree removal

    Dead oaks, poplars and leaning pines brought down safely and cleaned up.

    Price it

  • Storm debris cleanup

    Trees down after ice or wind cut, cleared off fences and roads, and mulched.

    Price it
